## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The new week opens with two competing forces in direct tension. On one side, a broad risk-on impulse is driving Asian equities to multi-year highs and pushing oil back above $93; on the other, the macro inflation backdrop is deteriorating with fresh urgency. US CPI stands at 3.95% YoY as of April [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL] and PPI at 2.66% MoM [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PPIACO], while the PCE inflation gauge hit a three-year high in April, with inflation jumping to 3.8% in April compared with a year ago (up from 3.5% in March), driven overwhelmingly by energy costs tied to the Strait of Hormuz closure [Source: https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/05/30/inflation-economy-gas-trump-mortgage-iran-unemployment/].

The critical development since Saturday's report is the Reuters June 1 story confirming the dollar held steady in Asia on Monday morning as markets awaited Iran war developments. Joseph Capurso, head of FX at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, is now on record flagging May NFP as the week's co-equal catalyst alongside Iran: "USD will be heavily influenced by developments in the US-Iran war and the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for May" [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/dollar-steadies-markets-await-signals-iran-war-central-banks-2026-06-01/]. The DXY settled at 99.036 after a weekly loss of approximately 0.4%, having previously benefited as a safe-haven at the war's outbreak [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/dollar-steadies-markets-await-signals-iran-war-central-banks-2026-06-01/].

Oil price action is the clearest signal of today's recalibration. After May closed with Brent suffering its largest monthly drop since 2020 on peace deal optimism — with both Brent and WTI settling near $91–$87 respectively — the new month opens with a sharp bid: Brent at $93.05 (+1.09%) and WTI at $89.64 (+2.61%) [Source: Yahoo Finance (BZ=F, CL=F)]. The OilPrice.com "Iran War's First 90 Days" retrospective notes that the ongoing Strait of Hormuz instability "continued to reshape shipping routes, energy trade patterns, and pricing dynamics throughout May," with late-month reports of a draft peace framework pushing prices sharply lower before the current recovery [Source: https://oilprice.com/Energy/Energy-General/The-Iran-Wars-First-90-Days-Upended-Energy-Markets.html]. A supermajor's warning that prices could hit $160/bbl remains live if negotiations fail.

Federal Reserve policy is entering a new phase of complexity. Multiple officials used the Iceland conference last Friday to signal that rate hikes — not merely holds — are on the table if energy-driven inflation proves persistent. Governor Bowman explicitly stated she would "consider shifting my approach to thinking about the balance of risks" contingent on whether the Iran war leads to a persistent inflation increase, while Chair Kevin Warsh has expressed skepticism about using balance sheet policy as augmentation [Source: https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-05-29/fed-officials-mull-raising-rates-curb-growing-inflation-risk]. This is a material shift from the prior "policy is in a good place" posture and directly elevates Friday's NFP as a Fed-sensitivity event. Social Security's 2027 COLA will now be determined by CPI-W data through Q3 2026, creating a political dimension to the inflation trajectory that constrains the White House's room for fiscal expansion [Source: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/05/31/trump-and-kevin-warsh-plan-a-huge-giveaway-to-retirees-theres-only-one-problem/].

Asian equity markets are today's standout story. The KOSPI has surged 4.58% to 8,864.27 — an extraordinary move reflecting both regional risk appetite and specific Korean semiconductor exposure — while the Nikkei has added 1.07% to reach 67,038 for the first time [Source: Yahoo Finance (^KS11, ^N225)]. The ASX 200 is a modest outlier, slipping 0.13% to 8,720.10 [Source: Yahoo Finance (^AXJO)], likely reflecting sector rotation rather than a macro divergence. European and US equity futures, based on Friday's closes of S&P 500 at 7,580.06 and DAX at 25,104.70, will take their cue from Asia's strength and Iran news flow as European hours open.

### Key Upcoming Catalysts — Week of June 1–6, 2026

1. **US-Iran Ceasefire Negotiations — Ongoing**: Reuters confirmed this morning that the dollar and all risk assets remain "heavily influenced by developments in the US-Iran war." The White House's conditions (uranium disposal, nuclear renouncement, full Hormuz reopening) define the binary. [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/dollar-steadies-markets-await-signals-iran-war-central-banks-2026-06-01/]

2. **May Non-Farm Payrolls — Friday, June 6**: Consensus expects ~96,000 jobs growth and unemployment rising to 4.3% — a significant deceleration. A miss deepens the stagflation narrative; a beat raises Fed hike probability. This is now the co-equal USD catalyst alongside Iran for the week. [Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/dollar-steadies-markets-await-signals-iran-war-central-banks-2026-06-01/]

3. **ECB Rate Decision — Wednesday, June 11**: Markets pricing 91% probability of a 25bp hike to 2.25% deposit rate; 50% probability of a September follow-up. ECB forward guidance language on the pace of further tightening will drive EUR/USD and DAX. [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/29/the-ecb-is-debating-rate-hikes-but-the-private-sector-could-help-out.html]

4. **EIA Weekly Crude Oil & Natural Gas Inventories — June 3–4**: US crude and gasoline inventories have been drawing sharply throughout the Hormuz crisis. Another significant drawdown would reinforce supply tightness and support oil's Monday recovery.

5. **China Caixin PMI — This Week**: China's manufacturing and services PMI releases will be critical for AUD, copper, and the broader Asian equity complex — especially given today's extraordinary KOSPI surge that may have partially anticipated a strong China print.
